grammar.note: Spaß machen = to be fun. Viel Spaß! = Have fun!

example_source: The game is a lot of [[fun]] for me.

grammar.note: A stronger form of nie.
No plural in this sense; die Schulden means debts.
Always with a direct object (a place or person). sich verlassen auf + accusative = to rely on.

example_target: Er [[verlässt]] das Haus um acht Uhr.
example_source: He [[leaves]] the house at eight o’clock.

grammar.note: etwas ernst nehmen = to take something seriously.

example_target: Das ist ein schöner [[Ort]] zum Leben.
example_source: This is a nice [[place]] to live.

grammar.note: auf der einen Seite ... auf der anderen Seite = on the one hand ... on the other hand.

example_target: Schlagt bitte das Buch auf [[Seite]] zwölf auf.
example_source: Please open the book at [[page]] twelve.

grammar.note: Dative for position (wo?), accusative for movement (wohin?).

example_target: Die Bank ist [[zwischen]] der Post und dem Café.
example_source: The bank is [[between]] the post office and the café.

grammar.note: Also a particle: Das ist eben so = That’s just the way it is. As an adjective: flat, level.
Colloquially also with the dative. As a conjunction: while (the verb goes to the end).
Pronounced the French way, roughly "SHAHN-se".
meine Freundin often means "my girlfriend"; eine Freundin von mir = a friend of mine.

example_target: Mein Großvater hat oft vom [[Krieg]] erzählt.
example_source: My grandfather often talked about the [[war]].

grammar.note: sich entschuldigen (bei + dative, für + accusative) = to apologize.
ins Bett gehen = to go to bed.
Mir ist schlecht = I feel sick.
On its own it means "Sorry!" or "Excuse me!".
die Wörter = individual words; die Worte = words as a statement (seine letzten Worte).
Colloquial for a man. Er ist nicht mein Typ = He’s not my type.

example_target: Der [[Typ]] da drüben ist echt nett.
example_source: That [[guy]] over there is really nice.

grammar.note: Subordinating: the verb goes to the end.

example_target: Nimm einen Schirm mit, [[falls]] es regnet.
example_source: Take an umbrella [[in case]] it rains.

grammar.note: Also a particle in warnings: Pass bloß auf! = Just be careful! As an adjective: bare.

example_source: I [[only]] have ten euros on me.

grammar.note: For location (wo?); for direction use nach unten.
das Teil = a part or component; zum Teil = partly.

example_target: Der erste [[Teil]] des Films war gut.
example_source: The first [[part]] of the film was good.

grammar.note: To put something upright (legen = to lay flat). eine Frage stellen = to ask a question.

example_target: Ich [[stelle]] die Flasche auf den Tisch.
example_source: I [[put]] the bottle on the table.

grammar.note: With plural nouns: a few, several; with singular nouns: some (einige Zeit).
Colloquial for bekommen.
No plural.
Ehrlich? = Really?
Plural only (die Eltern); one parent is ein Elternteil.
With zu + infinitive: to seem (Er scheint müde zu sein).
Irregular: genitive des Herzens, dative dem Herzen.
Auf Wiedersehen! = Goodbye! (polite). As a noun: a reunion.
Morgen habe ich frei = I have tomorrow off.
so schnell wie möglich = as quickly as possible.
Das reicht! = That’s enough! jemandem etwas reichen = to pass someone something.

example_source: Two pieces of cake [[are enough]] for me.

grammar.note: Also an adverb: fest schlafen = to sleep soundly. das Fest = the festival.
Colloquially shortened to irgendwas.
Platz nehmen = to take a seat; Platz haben = to have room.
Informal; the neutral word is Vater.
Only after a negative: nicht ... sondern. nicht nur ... sondern auch = not only ... but also.
Mostly for phone, house or room numbers; a number in maths is die Zahl.
Comparative of früh. As an adjective: former (mein früherer Chef).
For direction; for location use wo.
außer Betrieb = out of order.
morgen früh = tomorrow morning.
sich setzen = to sit down (a movement); sitzen = to be sitting.
Also an adjective: likely, probable.
Not used for "You’re welcome" (that is Bitte! or Gern geschehen!).
Also a map: der Stadtplan = the city map.

example_source: Do you have a [[plan]] for tomorrow?

grammar.note: Direction towards the speaker (wohin?); for location use hier.
After a number it stays Dollar: zehn Dollar.
Passt dir Montag? = Does Monday suit you? passen zu + dative = to go with.
Superlative of nah (near); always inflected: der nächste Bus, nächstes Jahr.
eine Menge = a lot (of).

example_source: The bus is going very [[slowly]] today.

grammar.note: More formal than schon.

example_target: Ich bin bis fünf Uhr im [[Büro]].
example_source: I’m in the [[office]] until five o’clock.

grammar.note: To phone someone is anrufen.
In the sense "to create" it is strong: schuf, hat geschaffen.
Usually no plural. Colloquially: Das war die Hölle! = That was hell!

example_target: Die Hitze im Büro war die [[Hölle]].
example_source: The heat in the office was [[hell]].

grammar.note: At the start of a clause the verb comes next: Trotzdem gehen wir.

example_target: Es regnet, aber wir gehen [[trotzdem]] spazieren.
example_source: It’s raining, but we’re going for a walk [[anyway]].

grammar.note: Colloquial for Arzt; also the title Dr.

example_source: I have to go to the [[doctor]] tomorrow.

example_target: Gibt es einen [[direkten]] Zug nach Wien?
example_source: Is there a [[direct]] train to Vienna?

grammar.note: A queen is die Königin.

example_target: Wir essen und gehen [[danach]] ins Kino.
example_source: We’ll eat and [[afterwards]] go to the cinema.

grammar.note: For machines and plans; a person works = arbeiten.
The verb comes right after it: deswegen bin ich ...

example_target: Ich war krank, [[deswegen]] bin ich nicht gekommen.
example_source: I was ill, [[that’s why]] I didn’t come.

grammar.note: Mixed verb: nannte, hat genannt.
Hast du Feuer? = Have you got a light?

example_source: We’re making a [[fire]] in the garden.

grammar.note: sich erinnern an + accusative = to remember. Without sich: jemanden an etwas erinnern = to remind someone of something.

example_target: Ich [[erinnere mich]] nicht an seinen Namen.

grammar.note: Also an adjective: complete, total.
an deiner Stelle = if I were you; eine neue Stelle = a new job.
Colloquial; plural also die Kumpels.

example_target: Er ist ein alter [[Kumpel]] von mir.

grammar.note: The plural die Lüfte is rare and literary.
Meaning "to move (house)" it takes sein: Wir sind nach Berlin gezogen.
Verschwinde! = Get lost! (rude).
aufhören mit + dative, or aufhören zu + infinitive = to stop doing something.
Always inflected before a noun: mein eigenes Auto.
zwar ... aber = it’s true ... but; und zwar = namely, to be precise.

example_target: Das Hotel ist [[zwar]] teuer, aber schön.
example_source: The hotel is [[admittedly]] expensive, but nice.

grammar.note: sich fühlen = to feel (well, ill, tired): Wie fühlst du dich?
Used with sein after the noun: etwas wert sein. Das ist es wert = It’s worth it.
A female doctor is die Ärztin.

example_source: I have to go to the [[doctor]] today.

example_target: Ich bin [[froh]], dass du da bist.

grammar.note: Takes a direct object, without "mit": Sie heiratet ihn.
Colloquial and never inflected: ein super Film.
Colloquially very common as an adverb: total gut = really good.
Plural die Partys (not -ies). A political party is die Partei.

example_source: Are you coming to the [[party]] on Saturday?

grammar.note: Takes the dative: Vertrau mir! = Trust me! das Vertrauen = trust.

example_source: [[Back then]] there were no mobile phones.

grammar.note: Also light (not heavy): ein leichter Koffer.
Subordinating: the verb goes to the end; usually with the pluperfect.

example_target: [[Nachdem]] wir gegessen hatten, gingen wir spazieren.
example_source: [[After]] we had eaten, we went for a walk.

grammar.note: sich interessieren für + accusative = to be interested in.
After a number it stays Stück: zwei Stück Kuchen. Also a play (Theaterstück).

example_source: Would you like a [[piece]] of cake?

grammar.note: genauso ... wie = just as ... as.
Usually no plural. Also the future tense.

example_target: In der [[Zukunft]] möchte ich in Spanien leben.
example_source: In the [[future]] I’d like to live in Spain.

grammar.note: die Nachrichten = the news (on TV or radio).
Usually da drüben or dort drüben.
sich kümmern um + accusative. Das kümmert mich nicht = I don’t care about that.
Also a preposition: laut Wetterbericht = according to the weather forecast.
Takes the accusative: Ich rufe dich an.
A position; to sit down is sich setzen. In southern Germany and Austria: ist gesessen.

example_target: Wir [[sitzen]] im Garten und trinken Kaffee.
example_source: We’re [[sitting]] in the garden drinking coffee.

grammar.note: Usually no plural.

example_target: Die [[Erde]] dreht sich um die Sonne.

grammar.note: die Reste often means leftovers.
Comparative of bald: je eher, desto besser = the sooner, the better.

example_target: Das alte [[Gefängnis]] ist heute ein Museum.
example_source: The old [[prison]] is a museum today.

grammar.note: Also a sacrifice: ein Opfer bringen.
